clue.text: Mrs Woolf concerned herself with his room, as well as her own

definitions.text: Mrs Woolf concerned herself with his room, as well as her own

parts.words: Mrs Woolf concerned herself with his room, as well as her own
parts.note: Virginia Woolf wrote a novel named after a young man's room, and the essay A Room of One's Own

explanation.surface: Virginia Woolf takes an interest in a man's room as well as her own.
explanation.definitionFit: Woolf's 1922 novel is titled after this character's room, so he is the owner of the room she wrote about.

clue.text: Wiltshire writer said to be bad judge

indicators.note: said to be tells us the writer's name is spoken like the name of the judge

parts.note: Judge Jeffreys was the notorious 'hanging judge' of the Bloody Assizes of 1685

explanation.surface: A writer from Wiltshire is reputed to be a poor judge.
explanation.walkthrough: Richard Jefferies wrote about the Wiltshire countryside; his surname is pronounced like that of George Jeffreys, the cruel seventeenth-century English judge.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Jefferies, the nature essayist, was born near Swindon in Wiltshire.

clue.text: Shelley's Beautiful Patricide, towards whom Clement was not

definitions.text: Shelley's Beautiful Patricide, towards whom Clement was not

parts.words: Shelley's Beautiful Patricide, towards whom Clement was not
parts.note: Shelley's verse tragedy concerns Beatrice, who killed her father; Pope Clement VIII refused to pardon her, so he was not clement towards her

explanation.surface: Shelley's lovely father-killer was shown no mercy by a pope.
explanation.walkthrough: Clement is the pope's name, and also the quality he did not show: he declined to spare Beatrice from execution in 1599.
explanation.definitionFit: Beatrice of that Roman family is the heroine of Shelley's play The Cenci, executed for murdering her father.

clue.text: Malcolm's quids in

explanation.surface: Malcolm is in the money.
explanation.walkthrough: Malcolm is the novelist Malcolm Bradbury; 'quids' are pounds, and old British pound notes were nicknamed after John Bradbury, whose signature they bore.
explanation.definitionFit: Belonging to novelist Malcolm Bradbury, and early-twentieth-century British pound notes signed by Treasury official John Bradbury.

clue.text: Small Florence crustaceans in Vaughan Williams work

parts.note: Flo is the short form of the name Florence
scampi are langoustines, a kind of shellfish

explanation.surface: Little Florence eats shellfish during a piece by Vaughan Williams.
explanation.definitionFit: Flos Campi is a 1925 suite for viola, chorus and orchestra by the English composer Ralph Vaughan Williams.

clue.text: Leonore in drag

parts.note: in Beethoven's only opera the heroine Leonore disguises herself as a young man to rescue her husband

explanation.definitionFit: This is the male alias Leonore adopts in Beethoven's opera, which also takes the alias as its title.

clue.text: Prokofiev wrote of affection for them

definitions.text: Prokofiev wrote of affection for them

parts.words: Prokofiev wrote of affection for them
parts.note: Prokofiev's comic opera is The Love for Three of these fruit

explanation.surface: A Russian composer wrote about his fondness for something.
explanation.definitionFit: Prokofiev's opera The Love for Three Oranges names these citrus fruit in its title.

clue.text: Jaques's justice was lined with a good one

definitions.text: Jaques's justice was lined with a good one

parts.words: Jaques's justice was lined with a good one
parts.note: in the Seven Ages speech of As You Like It, the justice has a fair round belly with good fowl lined

explanation.surface: A Shakespearean magistrate's stomach was well stuffed.
explanation.walkthrough: Jaques's speech describes the justice 'In fair round belly with good capon lined', a castrated cockerel fattened for the table.
explanation.definitionFit: A castrated cockerel fattened for eating, the bird that filled the justice's belly in Shakespeare's speech.

clue.text: I am in French upland surroundings to meet essayist

indicators.note: the clue's I says it is in, sitting within the next word
surroundings says the French word forms a ring around the single letter

parts.note: montagne is French for mountain

explanation.surface: Someone in the French hills goes to meet a writer of essays.
explanation.definitionFit: Michel de Montaigne, the sixteenth-century French writer, invented the essay form with his Essais.

clue.text: "Say that the Creator made — from designs by Michael Angelo" (Mark Twain)

definitions.text: "Say that the Creator made — from designs by Michael Angelo" (Mark Twain)

parts.words: "Say that the Creator made — from designs by Michael Angelo" (Mark Twain)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation from Twain's The Innocents Abroad, joking about the land of Renaissance art

explanation.walkthrough: In The Innocents Abroad Twain mocks guides who credit everything to Michelangelo, saying the Creator made this whole country from his designs.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mediterranean country of Michelangelo, which Twain toured and satirised in The Innocents Abroad.

clue.text: Reorchestrate (and fail) in patriotic suite

indicators.note: to reorchestrate is to arrange music anew, so these letters get a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A national suite is rescored, and it flops.
explanation.definitionFit: Sibelius's tone poem became an anthem of national pride for the Finns under Russian rule.

clue.text: Errant squire went out on his ass

definitions.text: Errant squire went out on his ass

parts.words: Errant squire went out on his ass
parts.note: Don Quixote's squire Sancho rode a donkey on their knight-errant adventures

explanation.surface: A wandering attendant rode off on a donkey.
explanation.definitionFit: Sancho's surname: he is Don Quixote's squire in Cervantes's novel, always riding his donkey.

clue.text: Israelite prince offered lamb (British?)

parts.note: Charles Lamb wrote his essays under the pen name Elia

explanation.surface: A Hebrew prince was given a lamb, possibly a British one.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Book of Numbers Eliab son of Helon leads the tribe of Zebulun, one of its chiefs.

clue.text: See a railway on foot -it's fabulous!

indicators.note: on places the railway after the foot piece, so it is written second

parts.note: the foot is the end of the leg, so foot gives leg end

explanation.surface: Seeing a railway while walking is marvellous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' puts A RY after the foot, cheekily read as the leg's end; 'See' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fabulous belongs to fable, the stuff of myth and storytelling.

clue.text: Deduce no Italian poem

parts.note: to deduce is to conclude by reasoning
taken as written

explanation.surface: Concluding that an Italian work is not a poem.
explanation.definitionFit: Dante's first cantica of the Divine Comedy, describing the descent through Hell.

clue.text: Cela entitled Pascual Duarte to be one

definitions.text: Cela entitled Pascual Duarte to be one

parts.words: Cela entitled Pascual Duarte to be one
parts.note: Camilo José Cela's novel is titled The Family of Pascual Duarte, so its hero has a household

explanation.surface: A Spanish novelist gave his hero a particular role.
explanation.definitionFit: A man with a household, wife and children, as Cela's title implies for Pascual Duarte.

clue.text: Parasites of Surtees hero

explanation.surface: Freeloaders belonging to a Victorian novel's hero.
explanation.walkthrough: R. S. Surtees wrote Mr Sponge's Sporting Tour, whose hero 'Soapey' Sponge lives off others; the second sense is the possessive of his name.
explanation.definitionFit: Hangers-on who live off others, and belonging to Soapey Sponge, the cadging hero of Surtees's hunting novel.

clue.text: 4 Down offered several such approaches

parts.note: Beethoven wrote four different orchestral openings for his single opera, and approaches also means advances

explanation.surface: An opera gave several advances.
explanation.definitionFit: Orchestral introductions to an opera; the word also means overtures of friendship, approaches made to someone.

clue.text: Aramaic dialect often described as good

explanation.surface: A Semitic tongue is usually praised.
explanation.definitionFit: The Western Aramaic speech of the people of Samaria, and the helpful traveller of Christ's parable.

clue.text: Spring gave us his circus

parts.note: the novelist Howard Spring wrote a children's book about a circus belonging to a man of this surname

explanation.surface: The season brought us a circus.
explanation.walkthrough: Spring is not the season but Howard Spring, the Welsh novelist, whose 1936 children's book is Sampson's Circus.
explanation.definitionFit: The ringmaster's surname in Howard Spring's children's book, whose circus the title names.

clue.text: The innocence of Rousseau

parts.note: Henri Rousseau, the self-taught painter, is the classic artist of the naive style

explanation.definitionFit: Artless simplicity, the untutored quality for which painter Henri Rousseau's jungle canvases are celebrated.

clue.text: Not Shakespeare's schoolboy, arriving thus prematurely

definitions.text: Not Shakespeare's schoolboy, arriving thus prematurely

parts.words: Not Shakespeare's schoolboy, arriving thus prematurely
parts.note: Jaques's schoolboy creeps unwillingly to school, so a keen pupil would come before lessons begin

explanation.surface: Unlike the reluctant boy in the play, someone turns up early.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as PRE-TERM: before the school term starts, the opposite of the schoolboy 'creeping like snail unwillingly to school' in As You Like It.
explanation.definitionFit: Born before full gestation; read in two halves it says ahead of the school's opening week.

clue.text: Unreliable staples of artists in crayons

indicators.note: something unreliable cannot be counted on to stay put, so these letters shift

explanation.surface: Artists who work in crayon have untrustworthy basic supplies.
explanation.definitionFit: Pictures drawn with chalky coloured sticks, the works of those who draw in crayon.

clue.text: Friend of Brutus could get lit up after five

indicators.note: after puts the shuffled word behind the Roman numeral

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five

indicators.note: could get suggests the letters might be made into something else

parts.note: luminous means lit up, shining

explanation.surface: A companion of Brutus might be illuminated after five o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could get' asks for a word meaning 'lit up' to be rearranged, not the words themselves; the result follows V, the Roman five.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's Julius Caesar this old schoolfellow of Brutus refuses to help him take his own life.

clue.text: Eloquent lyric

explanation.definitionFit: Outspoken and articulate, and relating to singing, as lyric verse is meant for song.

clue.text: Scene of French underground activity recorded by Queneau

definitions.text: Scene of French underground activity recorded by Queneau

parts.words: Scene of French underground activity recorded by Queneau
parts.note: Raymond Queneau's novel Zazie dans le ... features a girl longing to ride the Paris subway

explanation.surface: Where the French Resistance operated, as told by a novelist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Underground activity' suggests the wartime Resistance, but it is the Paris subway railway that Zazie wants to ride.
explanation.definitionFit: The Paris subway system, the title setting of Queneau's Zazie dans le métro, closed by a strike.

clue.text: Revolutionary bathing victim, unfortunately in West Country river

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things have gone wrong, so the name's letters are jumbled

parts.note: Jean-Paul Marat, French Revolutionary, was stabbed in his bath by Charlotte Corday

explanation.surface: A revolutionary in his bath meets a sad end in a western river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tamar forms most of the boundary between Devon and Cornwall in south-west England.

clue.text: Travis gets Military Cross, gracious!

parts.note: MC is the abbreviation for the Military Cross medal
gee is an exclamation of surprise, like 'gracious!'

explanation.surface: Travis is awarded a medal, goodness!
explanation.definitionFit: Travis McGee is the boat-dwelling detective of John D. MacDonald's novels, so the forename identifies him.

clue.text: A subject for sf "according to Hoyle"

definitions.text: A subject for sf "according to Hoyle"

parts.words: A subject for sf "according to Hoyle"
parts.note: the astronomer Fred Hoyle wrote science fiction, including a novel about Halley's celestial visitor

explanation.surface: A topic for science fiction, done by the rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'According to Hoyle' usually means by the rules of card games; here it is Fred Hoyle, astronomer and author of the novel Comet Halley.
explanation.definitionFit: An icy body with a glowing tail orbiting the sun, the subject of Fred Hoyle's 1985 novel.

clue.text: Annual medicine put to novel use by Susan Coolidge

definitions.text: Annual medicine put to novel use by Susan Coolidge

parts.words: Annual medicine put to novel use by Susan Coolidge
parts.note: a yearly herb used for sore eyes gave its name to a novel by the author of What Katy Did

explanation.surface: A yearly remedy is turned into fiction by an American author.
explanation.definitionFit: Euphrasia, an annual plant long used in herbal eye remedies, and the title of Susan Coolidge's 1879 novel.

clue.text: Capital creations of Maureen Duffy

parts.note: Maureen Duffy wrote a novel about the inhabitants of the English capital

explanation.surface: Excellent works by a British writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like praise but means the city: Duffy's 1983 novel is titled after its residents.
explanation.definitionFit: Residents of England's capital city, and the title of Maureen Duffy's 1983 novel.

clue.text: American author, in Paris, looks like a mug in Germany

explanation.surface: A US writer in France resembles a German beer mug.
explanation.walkthrough: Gertrude Stein, the American writer, lived in Paris; in German the word also names a beer mug.
explanation.definitionFit: Gertrude, the expatriate writer who hosted a Paris salon, and a stoneware beer tankard of German origin.
